title: The Battle of Badr (Yawm al-Furqan)
app_target: 3D Seerah learning app for ages 12-25 (interactive 3D scenes; battle timeline; verse overlays)

spine_source.work: Raheeq al-Makhtum (MSA NIU English ed.), Saifur Rahman al-Mubarakpuri, trans. Issam Diab (Dar-us-Salam)
spine_source.badr_chapter_pages: PDF pp. 132-147 (print page = PDF page in this edition)
spine_source.citation_format: Raheeq al-Makhtum (MSA NIU English ed.), p. N

conventions.block_tagging: Every app text block tagged HISTORY or REFLECTION. All ledger entries are HISTORY; reflections are generated in Phase 2 as separate REFLECTION blocks keyed to entry IDs.
conventions.honorifics: The Prophet is referenced as 'the Prophet (PBUH)' in rendered text; Companions carry (may Allah be pleased with them) at first mention per block. No figural depiction of the Prophet (PBUH), Companions, or identifiable named persons.
conventions.quote_cap: Direct on-screen quotes are <= 15 words. Quran text is fetched live from api.alquran.cloud at build time; hadith verifications recorded in live_verification_log.
conventions.no_harmonization: DISPUTED entries display ranges/both versions. UNKNOWN = not verifiable from owned + live canonical sources this session; hidden by default.
conventions.secondary_sirah: Ibn Hisham/Ibn Ishaq-derived claims are cited via Raheeq or online reproductions logged in live_verification_log; no full Guillaume translation is owned locally.

grading_policy.CERTAIN: >= 2 independent sources, at least one canonical (Quran > Sahih Bukhari/Muslim > other canonical collections > sirah Ibn Hisham/Ibn Ishaq, Ibn Sa'd, al-Tabari > modern critical works). Raheeq al-Makhtum alone never certifies.
grading_policy.REPORTED: Solid single-chain sirah/hadith detail; accurate to attribute but from one lineage or modern retelling only; rendered with no certainty implied.
grading_policy.DISPUTED: Transmitted variants conflict; app must show ranges/both versions, never harmonized.
grading_policy.UNKNOWN: Cannot be verified from owned + live sources; never rendered without user approval.

render_as_policy.solid: Canonical or >=2 independent sources; safe as primary on-screen facts, may carry direct quotes.
render_as_policy.approx: Reported or contested detail; render visually/ambiguously, quotes flagged, no Fame-of-truth framing.
render_as_policy.hidden: Do not render in current phase; visible only in an app 'scholar's mode' if the user approves.

entries.claim: A Quraish caravan returning from Syria, carrying some 50,000 gold dinars guarded by 40 men, passed near Madinah; scouts Talhah bin 'Ubaidullah (RA) and Sa'id bin Zaid (RA) had spotted it from al-Hawra' and reported back.

sources.quote: 50 thousand gold Dinars guarded by 40 men

entries.notes: Dinar figure and guard count from spine only; no independent verification this session. Opens the caravan-bait story.

entries.claim: The Prophet called the Muslims to intercept the caravan to recover their confiscated wealth; the call was voluntary, with no binding orders, framed as a small-scale errand.
entries.notes: Voluntariness matters ethically for the app; sirah-level framing.

entries.claim: Abu Sufyan (leader of the caravan) hired Damdam bin 'Amr al-Ghifari to race to Makkah; the messenger cut the camel's nose and ears, tore his shirt, and cried the alarm at the Ka'bah.

sources.quote: O Quraish! Your merchandise!

entries.notes: Sirah-drama beat; full speech not independently verified. Do not render as canon certifiable speech; visual panic scene is fine.

entries.claim: Quraish mustered almost all their forces to answer the alarm; sources disagree on size. Show both figures at muster and again in the field.

sources.quote: 1300 soldiers including 100 horsemen and 600 mailed soldiers
they were one thousand

variants.note: 1,300 marched out of Makkah; after Banu Zahrah withdrew Raheeq says 'the rest of the army, now 1000 soldiers' reached Badr.
Sahih Muslim 1763 numbers the polytheists at 1,000 on the day of battle.

entries.notes: Do not harmonize. App shows '1,300 set out; ~1,000 took the field' as range.

entries.claim: Camp-color detail on the Quraish march: camels slaughtered 'ten and nine' in alternate days for rations; fear of a Banu Bakr raid on their rear; Abu Lahab stayed behind, delegating a debtor; Banu 'Adi clan did not consent to mobilize.
entries.notes: Texture only; safe but non-essential. Kept out of default render.

entries.claim: Iblis appeared to Quraish in the guise of Suraqa bin Malik bin Ju'sham al-Mudlaji, chief of Kinana, guaranteeing no harm from behind; the Quran labels this satanic assurance (8:47, 8:48). At battle's collapse the devil-figure fled and plunged into the sea.

sources.quote: I guarantee that no harm will happen from behind

variants.note: The identification of the satan-figure with Suraqa is Ibn Ishaq/Ibn Hisham sirah detail; the Quran only says Satan said 'no one will overcome you today'.

entries.notes: Render the satan-voice scene via 8:48 overlay; keep the Suraqa-guise identification as app-side soft narration flagged as sirah detail.

entries.claim: Abu Sufyan took the caravan off the main route toward the Red Sea coast and slipped past Madinah; a second messenger then reached the Quraish army telling it to return since the caravan was safe.

sources.quote: inclined it towards the Red Sea

entries.notes: Key plot twist explaining why the battle happened at all; sirah-level, universally retold.

entries.claim: Abu Jahl insisted the army proceed to Badr, stay three nights for festivities, and punish the Muslims; pride and caravan security framed as his motive.

sources.quote: stay three nights there for making festivities

entries.notes: 3-night festivals claim is Ibn Ishaq-chain sirah; keep soft-flagged.

entries.claim: Banu Zahrah broke away and returned to Makkah on the advice of al-Akhnas bin Shuraiq; Banu Hashim nearly left with them but stayed under Abu Jahl's threats. This left roughly 1,000 in the field.
entries.notes: Pairs with BADR-004 range display; 'well-rubbed palm tree' idiom about Akhnas kept out of HUD.

entries.claim: The Muslim army numbered roughly 300-319: eighty-two to eighty-six Emigrants plus 61 Aws and 170 Khazraj per Raheeq; canonical narrations give 'over 60' Emigrants, 'over 240/249' Ansar, 'over 310' total, and 319 exact in Sahih Muslim. Render 'about 313' with an on-request range.

sources.quote: 300- 317 men, 82- 86 Emigrants, 61 from Aws and 170 from Khazraj
the Emigrant warriors were over sixty (men) and the Ansar were over 249
his own Companions were three hundred and nineteen

variants.note: Bukhari 3959 (live-verified): 'warriors of Badr were over three-hundred-and-ten, as many as the Companions of Saul' - ties letter to 2:249 river test.
sunnah.com English prints 'over 249' for Bukhari 3956; Arabic text reads 'over 240' (nayyifan wa-arba'in wa-mi'atayn).
8:43 anchor: enemy shown 'few' in dream; 8:42: both parties at the 'Udwat sides.

entries.notes: Crowning variant cluster of the battle. Never display a single confident total; default label 'about 313 (sources range 310-319)'.

entries.claim: The army was lightly equipped: only two horses (Az-Zubair bin Al-'Awwam (RA) and Al-Miqdad bin Al-Aswad Al-Kindi (RA)), 70 camels shared one to each two or three men; the Prophet (PBUH), 'Ali and Murthid bin Abi Murthid al-Ghanawi shared a single camel.

variants.note: Earlier draft of this ledger wrongly said Abu Lubabah shared the camel; the spine names Murthid bin Abi Murthid al-Ghanawi. Corrected 2026-10-22.

entries.notes: Show 2 horses / 70 camels caption; shared-camel trip used in march vignette.

entries.claim: Deputies over Madinah during the campaign: first Ibn Umm Maktum, later Abu Lubabah bin 'Abdul-Mundhir.
entries.notes: Logistics; keep in scholar's mode only.

entries.claim: Command structure: general leadership Mus'ab bin 'Umair (RA) with a white standard; Emigrant battalion standard raised by 'Ali bin Abi Talib (RA); Helpers' standard in the hand of Sa'd bin Mu'adh (RA); right flank Az-Zubair (RA), left flank Al-Miqdad (RA), rear Qais bin Abi Sa'sa'ah (RA).
entries.notes: Banners colored white; flank commanders labeled on unit cards.

entries.claim: Emergency council on the road: Abu Bakr (RA) and 'Umar (RA) pledged obedience; Al-Miqdad (RA) vowed faithfulness ('we will not say as the Children of Israel did'); Sa'd bin Mu'adh (RA) spoke for the Helpers with full commitment; the Prophet (PBUH) then said to advance and be of good cheer.

sources.quote: Forward and be of cheer, for Allâh has promised me one of the two

variants.note: Al-Miqdad: 'Proceed where Allâh directs you to, for we are with you... if you were to take us to Bark Al-Ghimad, we will still fight resolutely with you.'
Sa'd: 'if you were to ask us to plunge into the sea, we will do that most readily and not a man of us will stay behind.'
Council scene is Ibn Ishaq/Ibn Hisham chain; canonical support for morale climate exists via 8:5-6 but not this dialogue.

entries.notes: Centerpiece scene; render speeches as in-world dialogue tagged HISTORY with 'sirah narration' footnote; the 'seek the Helpers' pledge is the pivot.

entries.claim: Battle-date: Raheeq pins the pre-battle night as Friday night, Ramadan 17th, year 2 AH; al-Anfal's revelation is tied to Badr, Ramadan 17th in the same source. Other transmitted dates (e.g., 12/16/19 Ramadan) circulate in the literature but were not independently verified from owned sources this session.

sources.quote: That was Friday night, Ramadan 17th., the year 2 A.H.

variants.note: Ramadan 17, 2 AH as default (spine).
Alternative dates cited across later sources; unverified here, treat as open question for map chronology.

entries.notes: Display 'Ramadan 2 AH' divider with 'commonly 17 Ramadan' caption; do not hard-brand Friday.

entries.claim: Route: army marched on the main road toward Makkah, turned left toward Badr; at as-Safra' two scouts were sent to locate the caravan. Return journey stops attested: the spoils divided at a large sand-hill after Badr; two prisoners executed at as-Safra'; reception at ar-Rawha'.

variants.note: Prior-session live geography: madainproject ~120 km; Wikipedia ~130 km; Saudipedia 150 km distance claims; full station lists differ by source and are flagged unverified.

entries.notes: Map shows only spine-attested points: Madinah, al-Hawra' (scouts), as-Safra', ar-Rawha', Badr. Intermediate stations would need Ibn Hisham/Guillaume verification first.

entries.claim: Distance Madinah to Badr: roughly 115-150 km depending on source (crow-flight vs road). App map uses a 120-150 km band with a note.

variants.note: ~120 km (madainproject); ~130 km (Wikipedia); 150 km (Saudipedia).

entries.notes: Range only; no single figure asserted on screen.

entries.claim: Near Badr the Prophet (PBUH) and Abu Bakr (RA) scouted ahead, questioning an old bedouin; later 'Ali (RA), Az-Zubair (RA) and Sa'd bin Abi Waqqas (RA) found two Quraish water-carriers. Some Muslims beat the boys into lying about the caravan, and the Prophet (PBUH) rebuked them; the truthful answers then revealed enemy strength, position and notables.

sources.quote: On telling the truth, you beat them, and on telling a lie, you released them!

entries.notes: ID inserted late (suffix A) to preserve stable anchor mappings. Strong ethics beat: truth versus convenience.

entries.claim: That night rain fell on both sides: it held back the polytheists but refreshed and steadied the Muslims; the army advanced a little and camped on the farther bank of the valley.
entries.notes: Weather layer: rain particle burst on both camps; 8:11 overlay explains 'cleansed them and removed the stain of Satan'.

entries.claim: The Prophet (PBUH) halted at the nearest spring of Badr; al-Hubab bin al-Mundhir (RA) asked whether this spot was Divine instruction or war-stratagem, then advised seizing the nearest wells, building a water basin, and stopping up all other wells; the plan was approved and executed at midnight.

sources.quote: Has Allâh inspired you to choose this very spot?
It is stratagem of war and consultation
encamp on the nearest water well and make a basin

entries.notes: Water-control mission step (AI note: playable objective). Ibn Hisham parallel verified only via online reproduction, not owned copy.

entries.claim: Sa'd bin Mu'adh (RA) proposed building a trellis hut ('arish) as the Prophet's (PBUH) headquarters and led a guards squad of Helpers to defend it.
entries.notes: 'Arish footprint + Sa'd standing guard outside; include later Masjid al-'Arish note via glossary only.

entries.claim: The Prophet (PBUH) spent the night in supplication; in a tent, whether inside armor per Bukhari or walking mantled per Muslim, he begged Allah to fulfill His promise, crying that if this small band perished none would worship Him on earth; Abu Bakr (RA) steadied him; then he went out reciting 54:45.

sources.quote: O Allah, accomplish for me what Thou hast promised to me
O Allah! I ask you the fulfillment of Your Covenant and Promise.
O Allah, if this small band of Muslims is destroyed

variants.note: Bukhari 2915 sets the prayer in a tent while clad in armor; Muslim 1763 has the mantle slipping from his shoulders as he faces the Qiblah, and Abu Bakr replacing it.
8:9 answered this prayer with a thousand succeeding angels; 54:45 recited on emerging.

entries.notes: Emotional core scene: audio du'a, cloak-fix beat, forest-wall audio of 'their assembly will be defeated'.

entries.claim: Standing orders before the clash: no man starts fighting until the Prophet's (PBUH) final word; arrows to be used to hold the enemy off rather than spent rashly, and the sword only at close quarters.

sources.quote: He recommended that they use their arrows sparingly

entries.notes: Tactical brief card pre-battle; arrow reserves as game mechanic justified by canonical hadith refs recorded earlier session.

entries.claim: At dawn the Prophet (PBUH) drew up the army in ranks, arranging them while holding an arrow; the enemy lines formed opposite at al-'Udwat al-Quswa.

sources.quote: pointing with an arrow which he held in his hand

entries.notes: Formation stage; standard-bearers placed per BADR-013.

entries.claim: A few Quraish men approached to draw water at Badr and were shot dead; only Hakim bin Hizam was spared, later celebrated for his conversion. 'Umair bin Wahab al-Jumahi reconnoitered and reported the Muslims Numbered ~300 and would fight to the last; the report weakened some Quraish will until Abu Jahl counter-campaigned on Nakhlah vengeance.
entries.notes: First-blood beat; 'draw-water party killed' severity flagged; keep long-range description minimal on screen.

entries.claim: Abu Jahl likewise prayed for victory against whichever party had abused kinship or brought what they did not know; the Quran answers via 8:19 that the judgment had already come.

sources.quote: Our Lord, whichever of the two parties was less kind to his relatives

entries.notes: Parallel-prayers moment; dramatic irony explicit when 8:19 plays over the enemy lines.

entries.claim: When the two sides came within sight, the Prophet (PBUH) supplicated that the conceited and haughty Quraish were defying Allah and His Messenger and asked for the promised victory.

sources.quote: O Allâh these are the haughty and conceited

entries.notes: Same du'a motif recurs at muster-departure (p.133) and at battle-edge (p.136); keep one version on screen.

entries.claim: First blood: al-Aswad bin 'Abdul-Asad al-Makhzumi stepped out vowing to drink from the Muslims' basin or destroy it; Hamzah (RA) cut down his leg and killed him inside the basin.
entries.notes: Challenger-right beat leading directly into the 3v3 duel.

entries.claim: A 3-v-3 duel: Quraish sent 'Utbah, Shaybah and al-Walid bin 'Utbah; a first Ansari trio ('Awf and Mu'awwidh sons of al-Harith plus 'Abdullah bin Rawahah (RA)) was rejected, and the Prophet (PBUH) sent Hamzah (RA), 'Ali (RA) and 'Ubaydah bin al-Harith (RA); Hamzah killed Shaybah, 'Ali killed al-Walid, and Hamzah finished 'Utbah after 'Ubaydah was gravely wounded; the Quran accent of killing-at-the-duel is tied to 22:19.

sources.quote: they were those who fought on the day of Badr
Hamzah killed Shaibah, while ‘Ali killed Al-Waleed

variants.note: Third Muslim champion recorded as 'Ubaida or Abu 'Ubaida bin al-Harith in Bukhari 3965; Ibn Majah 2835 (Sahih, verified earlier session) names 'Ubaydah b. al-Harith.
Raheeq adds: 'Ubaydah carried off with a leg cut off; died four or five days later (bile-duct disease); attribution detail sirah-level.

entries.notes: Duel is the signature slow-motion beat; name the opponent pairing Hamzah/Shaybah, 'Ali/Walid with certainty; 'Ubaydah/wound-arc flagged approx.

entries.claim: In the same chain, 'Ali (RA) said he would be the first to kneel before Allah for judgment on the Resurrection, which confirms his own duel-stand; rendered as his pre-duel vow in scene language.

sources.quote: I shall be the first man to kneel down before

entries.notes: Use as 'Ali's character-establishing line; keep as later recollection not an on-the-spot prophecy.

entries.claim: A sixteen-year-old named 'Umair flung away his dates, saying they held him back from Paradise, and plunged into the fight and died.

sources.quote: These (the dates) are holding me back from Paradise.

variants.note: Full clan-name of the youth is not given in these pages; avoid inventing a surname on screen.

entries.notes: The 'dates dropped' youth-driven scene; resonance with young target audience (12-25).

entries.claim: Ibn 'Abbas (RA) reported that a fleeing Maker heard a whip-swish and a voice 'Go ahead, Haizum!' before a pagan fell with whip-like wounds; the Prophet (PBUH) confirmed 'this was the help from the third heaven', the angels' entrance (8:9).

sources.quote: Go ahead, Haizum!
This was the help from the third heaven.

variants.note: Mishkat 5874 (notes from earlier session) explains Haizum as the name of the rider's horse; the hadith itself does not name the subject.

entries.notes: Angels rendered only as motion/whip-cracks and wind, never figures; sound-led beat.

entries.claim: Al-'Abbas (RA), captured by a Helper, insisted no one had seen his captor: 'a bald man with a handsome face riding a piebald horse'; the Prophet (PBUH) said Allah had aided that Helper through a noble angel.

variants.note: The famous 'Abbas-invisible-angel retelling possibly parallels canonical exchanges not re-examined this session; kept REPORTED until directly verified.

entries.notes: Keep interaction; angel presence stated by the Prophet's answer; no visual depicts the angel.

entries.claim: Ibn 'Abbas said the Prophet, on the day of Badr, pointed out Gabriel holding the head of his horse and equipped with weapons for battle.

sources.quote: This is Gabriel holding the head of his horse and equipped with arms

entries.notes: Never depict the angel; convey via shadow of wind, horse-breath audio, and narration only.

entries.claim: At the appointed moment the Prophet (PBUH) took a handful of gravel and cast it and cursed their faces; a violent sandstorm struck the enemy eyes, and 8:17 frames the throw as Allah's throw, not his.

sources.quote: Confusion seize their faces!

variants.note: Exact dhikr wording 'Confusion seize their faces!' not found in canonical hadith searched this session; gravel-throw act itself consistent with 8:17 vs Muslim 1763's throwing at Qiblah. Keep wording flagged.

entries.notes: Screen shows 8:17 as the certainty layer; the spoken line rendered low-mixed under dust FX with 'sirah narration' tag.

entries.claim: Only after this did the Prophet (PBUH) order a counter-attack, exhorting till they'd 'hasten to forgiveness', reciting 3:133 alongside manful reward-promise.

sources.quote: And be quick for forgiveness from your Lord

entries.notes: Transition beat into the mixed-mêlée phase.

entries.claim: The collapse: Quraish's ranks broke, and along with a sandstorm and divine sand the Prophet's (PBUH) old recital 'their assembly will be put to flight' (54:45-46, Bukhari 2915) was enacted.

sources.quote: There multitude will be put to flight and they will show their backs

variants.note: Abu Jahl also adjured his men by al-Lat and 'Uzza to stand firm; they scattered anyway; sirah beat.

entries.notes: Streaming updates: 'the predictions played out as men fled'; hide exact angelic detail behind FX.

entries.claim: Abu Jahl, abandoned though mounted, was slain by two young Helpers pointed out by 'Abdur-Rahman bin 'Awf (RA); they struck simultaneously, each claimed the kill, and the Prophet (PBUH) ruled both killed him when their swords showed blood; Raheeq names them Mu'adh bin 'Amr bin al-Jumuh and Mu'awwidh bin al-'Afra' (RA), with spoils going to Mu'adh because Mu'awwidh also fell in the same fight.

sources.quote: each claiming that he had killed Abu Jahl

sources.ref: cited by spine as Sahih Al-Bukhari 1/444, 2/568; Mishkat 2/352

variants.note: Separate canonical confirmation of BOTH swords showing blood was not re-verified independently via sunnah.com this session; the spine's own Bukhari bracket is untested here.

entries.notes: Names used only as attribution rows; faces/figures not shown.

entries.claim: Abdullah bin Mas'ud (RA) came across Abu Jahl breathing his last; Abu Jahl flatly denied being disgraced, saying he was not ashamed to be killed by his own folk. Raheeq continues with a duel of words, the beheading, and the Prophet's (PBUH) Ta'ala praise over the head before the well-throwing scene.

sources.quote: nor I am ashamed of being killed by my own folk.
You have followed difficult ways, you shepherd!

variants.note: Canonical Bukhari 3961 confirms the death-scene dialogue core (no shame line).
'You have followed difficult ways, you shepherd!' plus the Ibn Mas'ud-beheading and praise-words are Raheeq-text detail; canonical parallels not re-verified this session.

entries.notes: Split at render: canonical lines shown as subtitle canon; sirah extras sub-low-mixed.

entries.claim: Standing over Abu Jahl's body (brought, per Raheeq, after Ibn Mas'ud's beheading), the Prophet (PBUH) pronounced: 'This is the Pharaoh of this nation.'

sources.quote: This is the Pharaoh of this nation.

variants.note: Canonical search negative this session (name-space + page-1 Arabic pilot lookups); Ibn Hisham/Ibn Ishaq variants unverified; render only with sirah-narration flag if approved.

entries.notes: Sensitive echo line; keep optional.

entries.claim: The Prophet (PBUH) ordered sparing Banu Hashim combatants who were unreconciled to attend: al-'Abbas (RA) and Abu al-Bukhtari bin Hisham expressly named; Abu Hudhaifah bin 'Utbah (RA) begrudged the favor and 'Umar (RA) protected the Prophet-uncle's dignity; Abu al-Bukhtari nonetheless fell in combat with al-Mujdhir bin Ziyad al-Balwi.

sources.quote: By Allâh! If I see him I will surely strike him with my sword.

entries.notes: Spar-order beat ties to ethics panel; 'Abu Bukhtari' spelling pattern skip.

entries.claim: 'Umayyah bin Khalaf and his son were killed by a crowd after Bilal (RA) swore retribution for the torture he had suffered at 'Umayyah's hands; 'Abdur-Rahman bin 'Awf (RA), his old friend, was caught in the middle and pressed to give up his armour hope and escape.

sources.quote: May Allâh have mercy on Bilal, for he deprived me of the spoils

entries.notes: Torture-backstory tie-in to pre-Islam hazard story; keep muted on the brutality staging.

entries.claim: Kinship clashed: 'Umar (RA) slew even his maternal uncle al-'As bin Hisham; Abu Bakr (RA) shouted at his rebellious son 'Abdur-Rahman who answered the estate was 'gone with the wind'.

sources.quote: Where is my wealth, you wicked boy?

entries.notes: Paired beats; the father-son economy bar shows 'gone with the wind' as a comic-dark reflection.

entries.claim: The Prophet (PBUH), reading Sa'd bin Mu'adh's (RA) face after the kill, found him hostile to taking captives: Sa'd preferred slaying polytheists on the first Muslim victory over the polytheists.
entries.notes: Foreshadows the ransom-debate tug-of-war of BADR-050; link on HUD.

entries.claim: 'Ukashah bin Mihsan al-Asadi's (RA) sword broke; a log of wood given by the Prophet (PBUH) turned into a long strong white sword he carried in later conquests till the apostasy wars.
entries.notes: Miracle micro-beat; keep as 'sirah narration' ballad moment.

entries.claim: Mus'ab bin 'Umair (RA) met his captive polytheist brother Abu 'Aziz bound by an Ansari and told him to tighten the knot because the Helper was 'more eligible for brotherhood' than blood ties.

sources.quote: the Helper was more eligible for brotherhood than him

entries.notes: Aqeeqah-Amity line is a stage staple for the youth theme 'chosen brotherhood'.

entries.claim: Abu Hudhaifah bin 'Utbah (RA) looked sadly upon his dead polytheist father 'Utbah; he confessed his father met a deserved fate but grieved for lost guidance; the Prophet (PBUH) whispered comfort.
entries.notes: Whispered comfort is voiceless (no lip-sync of the Prophet); picture-of dignity with subtitle 'whispered'.

entries.claim: Muslim losses: fourteen martyrs - six from the Emigrants and eight from the Helpers.

sources.quote: Fourteen Muslims were killed

variants.note: Named casualties lists exist in later munk collections (e.g., Ibn Sa'd) not verified here; keep count generic on screen.

entries.notes: Martyrs' wall without names; count shown as '14 (6+8)'.

entries.claim: Polytheist losses: seventy killed and seventy captured - stated in both Sahih Muslim (through Ibn 'Umar) and Bukhari's Bara' narration (140 total casualties).

sources.quote: The Muslims that day killed seventy persons and captured seventy
70 were taken prisoners, and 70 were killed.

entries.notes: Headline counter rendered with two-source badge.

entries.claim: On the third day the Prophet (PBUH) rode out to the well into which the corpses of twenty-four leaders of Quraish had been thrown, called them by name and father's name, warned them that his Lord's promise had proven true, and answered 'Umar: 'You do not hear what I say better than they do.'

sources.quote: he used to stay at the battle-field for three nights
You do not hear, what I say better than they do.

variants.note: 24 leaders per Bukhari 3976; Muslim 2875 (per earlier session record) transmits 'more than twenty' - keep '24 (also reported >20)' in scholar's mode.
Raheeq adds the fuller address wording; use canonical fragments only.

entries.notes: Edgy scene for youth audience: 'dead hear better' line as canon-cert subtitle; no visual glorification.

entries.claim: Ransom Crisis: after capture, the Prophet (PBUH) asked Abu Bakr (RA) and 'Umar (RA) what should be done with 70 captives; Abu Bakr urged ransom ('they are our kith and kin'), 'Umar urged beheading; the Prophet preferred Abu Bakr's view, then both were found weeping the next day; revelation followed (8:67-69: rebuke for taking ransom too early + no torment for the previous ordainment 8:68), with Abu Hurayrah's (RA) narration warning that fire from heaven would have consumed earlier-ages capturers had no prior ordainment existed; 47:4 states the ransom-or-favor law gained by late revelation.

sources.quote: They are our kith and kin
hand them over to us so we may cut off their heads
I weep for what has happened to your companions for taking
fire from the heavens would be sent down upon them

entries.notes: The most adult scene of the arc; render ledger-style debate with both positions; no heroic framing of the behead idea.

entries.claim: In Muslim 1763 'Umar's plan names 'Aqil (the Prophet's cousin, 'Ali's brother) to be handed to 'Ali for beheading - implying 'Aqil stood among the Badr captives; other traditions locate 'Aqil's Islam much later, so his Badr-captive status is unresolved from sources at hand.

sources.quote: Hand over `Aqil to `Ali that he may cut off his head

variants.note: Whether 'Aqil was captured at Badr conflicts with his later conversion accounts; not resolvable without Ibn Sa'd/Ibn al-Kalbi collation.
sources: Sahih Muslim 1763 vs. sirah conversion chronologies

entries.notes: Do not render; scholar-mode footnote only.

entries.claim: Spoils crisis: fighters split into three claimant groups (those who seized goods, those who pursued the enemy, and those who guarded the Prophet (PBUH)); the Prophet (PBUH) deferred until revelation answered with 8:1.

sources.quote: We collected it, so no one else has any right to it.

sources.work: Sahih Muslim 1748b; Abu Dawud 2737 (verified earlier session)

variants.note: 'Ubadah bin as-Samit (RA) carries the narrative in Muslim's chain (verified earlier session); Raheeq's wording is a rendering of it.

entries.notes: Decision-freeze beat: HUD freezes loot cursor till 8:1 overlay lands.

entries.claim: At a large sand-hill the Prophet (PBUH) took the khums (one-fifth) and divided the rest equally among the fighters; 8:41 legislates the khums allocation.

sources.quote: divided the spoils equally among the fighters after he had taken Al-Khums (one-fifth)

entries.notes: Split-bar UI beat (1/5 to Allah's cause + 4/5 equal to fighters); 8:41 quote overlays.

entries.claim: Share-count dispute on the Emigrant share scale: Ibn Shihab reported 81 men of Quraish origin received shares; az-Zubair (RA) reported 100 shares for Emigrants; 'Urwa transmits az-Zubair as 'when distributed they came to 101'. Show both counts, never merge.

sources.quote: their number was 101 men. But Allah knows it better.

variants.note: 81 (Ibn Shihab / Qatada chain).
100 shares for Emigrants (az-Zubair direct).
101 split count ('Urwa from az-Zubair).

entries.notes: Classic variant display: three counts side-by-side with their chains; caption 'Allah knows better' kept.

entries.claim: 'Uthman bin 'Affan (RA) stayed in Madinah during Badr because his wife Ruqayyah, the Prophet's daughter, was ill; the Prophet (PBUH) granted him the reward and share equal to a fighter at Badr.

sources.quote: You will get a reward and a share (from the war booty)

variants.note: Ahmad's narration adds the absent one 'left her prayer?'-wording variant; the reward-share core stands on Bukhari 3130 alone plus Ahmad.

entries.notes: Compassion tune-in: absence-with-honor beat; ties to 062 chronology note.

entries.claim: On the return at as-Safra' the Prophet (PBUH) ordered two prisoners executed for earlier persecution: al-Nadr bin al-Harith and 'Uqbah bin Abi Mu'ayt; 'Uqbah's plea 'Who will look after my children?' was answered 'The fire (of Hell)'; Raheeq names 'Ali (RA) as the one who struck off both heads, and recounts 'Uqbah's earlier abuse (sheep-entrails, strangling cloak) as motive context.

sources.quote: Who will look after my children O Messenger of Allâh?
Who will look after my children?
Fire.

variants.note: Canonical chain (Abu Dawud 2686) ties the exchange wording as later quote from Ibn Mas'ud to 'Umarah b. 'Uqbah, not an on-field transcript.
as-Safra' setting, the execution order authority and 'Ali as executioner are Raheeq-level (Ibn Hisham chains noted historically but not re-verified).

entries.notes: War-crimes framing for 12-25 audience handled as sober history; no glee; parental-guidance flag on scene.

entries.claim: Al-Muṭ'im bin 'Adī interceded regarding ransom for Quraish captives per the canonical chain recorded earlier this phase.
entries.notes: Kept modest pending re-verification of exact wording; listed to honor earlier session's verified entry; not shown on default UI.

entries.claim: At ar-Rawha' the joyful Madinese met the army; Usaid bin Hudair (RA) excused not joining, thinking it a mere caravan errand, and the Prophet (PBUH) accepted his word.

sources.quote: if it had occurred to him that it would be real war

entries.notes: Crowd-scene beat preceding the conversions paragraph.

entries.claim: In Makkah, Ibn Ishaq names al-Haisaman bin 'Abdullah al-Khuza'i as the first bearer of the disaster news; Makkans refused to believe him, thinking him mad, until the report was confirmed.
entries.notes: Two-cities emotional divide set-point.

entries.claim: Abu Lahab, hearing the rout account toward Abu Rafi' (a reticent Muslim client) slapping him for the angels' mention; Umm al-Fadl (Lubabah bint al-Harith), enraged, struck him with a log cracking his head; seven days later he died of an ulcer, was left three days unburied, and his sons removed him at a distance and threw stones and dust at him.

sources.quote: died of an ominous ulcer

variants.note: Makkah mourning suppressed (wailing forbidden) so Muslims might not rejoice - context note; Ibn Sa'd has parallel chronicle texts not verified here.

entries.notes: Dark-comic famous beats; keep third-person, history-tagged.

entries.claim: To Madinah, two heralds - 'Abdullah bin Rawahah and Zaid bin Harithah (RA) - brought the victory news; rumours had spread (esp. among Jews and hypocrites) that the Prophet (PBUH) was killed, aided by Zaid riding al-Qaswa', the Prophet's she-camel.
entries.notes: Split-screen fear-to-joy beat on arrival.

entries.claim: Usamah bin Zaid related that the victory news reached Madinah shortly after Ruqayyah, the Prophet's daughter and wife of 'Uthman (RA), had been buried - she had been terminally ill, which is why 'Uthman stayed behind.
entries.notes: Chronology pairs with BADR-055; bittersweet beat; avoid rendering the word 'buried' before 055 in narrative order.

entries.claim: Prisoner welfare: the Prophet (PBUH) urged kindness so captors gave prisoners the bread and kept the dates - the valued part of the meal.

sources.quote: give the captives their bread (the more valued part of the meal)

entries.notes: Mercy-first beat; draft only if user keeps it - pairs with ransom-debate for moral arc.

entries.claim: Ransom mechanics claim-set: ransoms reportedly ranged 1,000-4,000 dirhams by the captive's able means; literate captives unable to pay were to teach ten Madinah children to read/write as ransom and poor captives were freed; these figures and teaching-ransom scheme come from Raheeq p.145 (Ibn Hisham chain unverifiable locally).

variants.note: Dirham range and 10-children literate-ransom: no canonical attestation located this session; a well-known Ibn Hisham report exists but not verified from an owned or live reproduction here.

entries.notes: Hold back until Guillaume/Ibn Hisham verification task; Quest for the app clarity requires an owner-approved recheck.

entries.claim: Zainab, the Prophet's daughter, sent her necklace as ransom for her husband Abul-'As bin ar-Rabi'; the Muslims released him and returned the necklace, on condition he let Zainab migrate to Madinah.
entries.notes: Family-ties story; keep his later conversion out-of-scope of this phase.

entries.claim: 'Umar proposed pulling out the front teeth of the captive orator Suhail bin 'Amr; the Prophet (PBUH) refused, lest Quraish retaliate in kind and to avert Allah's wrath on the Day of Resurrection.
entries.notes: Ethics-of-war micro-decision; pairs with BADR-050 debate color.

entries.claim: Sa'd bin an-Nu'man, a lesser pilgrim detained in Makkah, was exchanged for the release of Abu Sufyan's captive son.
entries.notes: Logistics foot-note; skip in default render.

entries.claim: First Shawwal after Badr coincided with the victory; Ramadan fasting was obligated in 2 AH and Eid al-Fitr landed directly after the triumph, read by Raheeq as 'a wonderful and striking coincidence' (8:26 ties the safety-to-grateful reflection).

sources.quote: directly after the manifest victory of Badr

entries.notes: Calendar overlay on timeline; date rendering flexible per BADR-015 disputes.

entries.claim: Al-Kudr expedition: in Shawwal 2 AH, seven days after Badr, the Prophet (PPUH) struck preemptively at Banu Saleem of Ghatafan mustering at al-Kudr; they fled, and 500 camels were taken as booty, split after khums at two camels per fighter.

sources.quote: seven days after the event of Badr

entries.claim: Later state policy: the Badr warriors received 5,000 dirhams each, yearly, with 'Umar (RA) vowing to prefer them over others.

sources.quote: The Badr warriors were given five thousand (Dirhams) each, yearly.

entries.notes: Treasury-ledger post-battle stat card.

entries.claim: The Prophet's (PBUH) sword Dhul-Fiqar came from Badr spoils (Ibn 'Abbas), graded Hasan by Darussalam.
